## Map of just the United Kingdom 
```{r}
#| label: fig-uk
#| fig-cap: "Basic Map of the UK"

world <- map_data("world")

UK_data <- world |>
  filter(region == "UK") 
# Like we did in class with CA, but since UK is not a state, I did world instead

UK_Map <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = UK_data,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group),
               fill = "pink", # the color you want the "state/country/whatever" to be filled with 
               color = "black") +
  coord_map() +
  theme_void()

UK_Map


```

@fig-uk I created a basic map of the United Kingdom. I filtered the world dataset to display only the UK. 

## Add the cat GPS observation - Map by individual cat
```{r}
Cat_Map_Trial <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = UK_data,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group),
               fill = "lightgray",
               color = "black") +
  geom_point(data = cats_uk,
             aes(x = location_long,
                 y = location_lat,
                 color = tag_id),
             size = 0.5) +
  coord_map() +
  theme_void()

Cat_Map_Trial
```

Okay so this looks a little **overwhelming**, I'm going to try plotting the data in a different way. Maybe by zooming in on the area where it was most recorded? 


## Join the two cat datasets 
```{r}
Cats_Combo <- cats_uk |>
  inner_join(cats_uk_reference, by = "tag_id")
```

I combined the two GPS tracking datasets using inner_join and using the "tag ID" column. 

## Mapping 
```{r}
#| label: fig-kitty-map
#| fig-cap: "GPS Locations of Cats by Reproductive Condition in the UK"

Kitty_Map <- ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = UK_data,
               aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
               fill = "#F8C8DC",
               color = "black") +
  geom_point(data = Cats_Combo,
             aes(x = location_long, y = location_lat,
                 color = animal_reproductive_condition),
             size = 1.2, alpha = 0.5) +
  coord_map(xlim = c(-6, -4), ylim = c(49.5, 51.5)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#2166ac", "#b2182b", "#4dac26","#7570b3")) +
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude",
       color = "Reproductive Condition") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "lightblue"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

Kitty_Map

ggsave(here("Week_07","Outputs","KittyMap.png"))
```
Okay, I think this looks much better! In @fig-kitty-map, I zoomed in on southwestern England so we can get a better look at where the cats were tracked. In this figure, I plotted the cats by their reproductive condition.
